newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AUTOLIV , MORTON UNIT TO MERGE.
newsitem.headline: AUTOLIV , MORTON UNIT TO MERGE.

text.p: Swedish automotive safety group Autoliv -- one of Europe's biggest airbag makers -- said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent with the car safety unit of U.S. company Morton International regarding a merger of the two companies.

"Autoliv and Morton International have signed a Letter of Intent intending to create a new automotive safety company through the merger of Mortons Automotive Safety Products (ASP) and Autoliv," Autoliv said in a statement.
It said the new operation would be the world's largest airbag and car safety company, with turnover of 20 billion crowns, 15,000 employees and wide-ranging operations in the U.S., Europe and Japan.

"The planned deal fits in perfectly with our strategy of attempting to strengthen Autoliv's position in the U.S. and Japan, where Morton's ASP already has a strong position," Autoliv president Paul Charlety said.
The merger would lead to the creation of a holding company, Autoliv Inc., whose head office would be in either Amsterdam or London, but whose legal domicile would be in the United States.

The merger is planned to take the form of a merger of equals, under which Autoliv AB's shareholders will exchange their shares for 53.5 percent of the shares in Autoliv Inc., and the shareholders in Morton International will exchange its ownership in ASP for 46.5 percent of the shares in Autoliv, Inc.
The board of the new company will initially consist of equal numbers from Autoliv AB and Morton International.
However, Gunnar Bark, who was Autoliv's Chief Executive Officer up to August 1996, will be chairman of the board, Autoliv said.
Fred Musone, currently president of Morton's ASP, will be CEO of the new company, while Paul Charlety will become chief operating officer, it said.
Immediately prior to the merger, Morton International will transfer its salt and specialty chemicals division to a new comapany which will take over the name Morton International.
The new company will also receive a capital injection of $750 million, which will be financed via new borrowing within ASP. The sum will thus become a liability within the Autoliv Inc group.
Morton International board chairman S Jay Stewart said in the statement the funds would be used for acquisitions and share buy-backs after the completion of the transactions.

The signing of the final agreement, which Autoliv said was expected to take place within six weeks, requires a satisfactory due dilligence investigation and the approval of the boards of both companies.
It will also require the approval of the majority of Morton International's shareholders as well as 90 percent of the shareholders in Autoliv AB.
